questions.q: A diatomic gas $( \gamma = 1 . 4 )$ does $200J$ of work when it is expanded isobarically. The heat given to the gas in the process is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For degree of freedom, we can write

$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = 1 . 4 ⇒ \dfrac{2}{f} = 0 . 4$

$⇒ f = 5$

For isobaric process, $W = nR\Delta T = 200J$.

Now, we can write

$Q = \left(\dfrac{f + 2}{2}\right)nR \Delta T$

$= \dfrac{7}{2} \times 200 = 700J$

questions.q: In an adiabatic process, which of the following statements is true?
options: The molar heat capacity is infinite
Work done by the gas equals the increase in internal energy
The molar heat capacity is zero
The internal energy of the gas decreases as the temperature increases
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For adiabatic process, $\mathrm{dQ}=0$
$\therefore$ Molar heat capacity $=0$
$\because \mathrm{dQ}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{dU}=-\mathrm{dW}$
Also $\mathrm{dU}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{2} \mathrm{nRdT}$
$\therefore$ Only option (3) is correct.

questions.q:
$n$~mole of a perfect gas undergoes a cyclic process $ABCA$~(see figure) consisting of the following processes.

$A \to B:$ Isothermal expansion at temperature $T$ so that the volume is doubled from ${V}_{1}$ to ${V}_{2} = 2{V}_{1}$ and pressure changes from ${P}_{1}$ to ${P}_{2}$
$B \to C:$ Isobaric compression at pressure ${P}_{2}$ to initial volume ${V}_{1} .$

$C \to A:$~Isochoric change leading to change of pressure from ${P}_{2}$ to ${P}_{1}$

Total work done in the complete cycle $ABCA$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${W}_{isothermal} = nRT ln \left(\dfrac{V2}{V1}\right)\

${W}_{isobaric} = P$\Delta$V = nR$\Delta$T$

${W}_{isochoric} = 0$

${W}_{1} = nRTln\left(\dfrac{2V}{V}\right) =$nRTln2$

${W}_{2} = nR\left(\dfrac{T}{2} -$T\right) = - nR$\dfrac{T}{2}

${W}_{3} = 0$

$⇒ {W}_{net} = {W}_{1} + {W}_{2} + {W}_{3}$

${W}_{net} = nRT \left(ln2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$

questions.q: A bicycle tyre is filled with air having pressure of $270$ kPa~at $27 ° C$. The approximate pressure of the air in the tyre when the temperature increases to $36 ° C$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& ${P}_{1} = 270kPa, {T}_{1} = 27 + 273 = 300K, {T}_{2} = 36 + 273 = 309K$

Ideal gas~equation is given by~$PV = nRT$.

Considering isochoric process, i.e., constant~volume~so~$P ∝ T$

Thus,~$\dfrac{P1}{T1} = \dfrac{P2}{T2}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} = \dfrac{P1}{T1} \times {T}_{2} = \dfrac{270 \times \left(309\right)}{300}$

$= 278kPa$

questions.q: In a process, temperature and volume of one mole of an ideal monoatomic gas are varied according to the relation $\mathrm{VT}=\mathrm{K},$ where $\mathrm{K}$ is a constant. In this process the temperature of the gas is increased by $\Delta \mathrm{T}$. The amount of heat absorbed by gas is (R is gas constant):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $According to question $\mathrm{VT}=\mathrm{K}$ we also know that $P V=n R T\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{nR}}\right)\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}\left(\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{nR}}\right)=\mathrm{k} \Rightarrow \mathrm{PV}^{2}=\mathrm{K}\because \mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{1-\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}$ (For polytropic process) $\mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{1-2}+\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\therefore \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{nC} \Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{R}{2} \times \Delta \mathrm{T}$ [here,  \left.\mathrm{n}=1 \mathrm{~mole}\right]$

questions.q: A monoatomic gas at pressure $P$ and volume $V$ is suddenly compressed to one eighth of its original volume. The final pressure at constant entropy will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in entropy is given by& $d S = \dfrac{d Q}{T}$. Since, the process is~$d S = 0$,~$d Q = 0$. Therefore, constant entropy means the process is adiabatic.

$PV^{γ} =$constant

$⇒ {P}_{1}{V}_{1}^{γ} = {P}_{2}{V}_{2}^{γ}$

For a monatomic gas~$\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ {P}_{1}{V}_{1}^{53} = {P}_{2}\left(\dfrac{V1}{8}\right)\dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ {P}_{1}{V}_{1}^{53} = \dfrac{{P}_{2}{V}_{1}^{\dfrac{5}{3}}}{32}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} = 32{P}_{1}$

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
\(
List - IList - II
(A)Isobaric(I)$\Delta$Q=$\Delta$W
(B)Isochoric(II)$\Delta$Q=$\Delta$U
(C)Adiabatic(III)$\Delta$Q= zero
(D)Isothermal(IV)$\Delta$Q=$\Delta$U+P $\Delta$V
\)
$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=$ Heat supplied
$\Delta \mathrm{W}=$ Work done by the system
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=$ Change in internal energy
$\mathrm{P}=$ Pressure of the system
$\Delta \mathrm{V}=$ Change in volume of the system
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Isobaric $(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{C})$
$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{U}+\mathrm{P} \Delta \mathrm{~V}$
(B) Isochoric $(\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{C})$
$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{U}$
(C) Adiabatic $(\Delta \mathrm{Q}=0)$
$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=0$
(D) Isothermal $(\Delta \mathrm{U}=0)$
$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{W}$

questions.q: For the given cyclic process $CAB$ as shown for a gas, the work done is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in a cyclic process is equal to the area of closed P-V curve cycle.

Work done,& $W =$~Area of~$∆ CAB$

$⇒ W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC= \dfrac{1}{2} \times ( 6 - 1 ) \times ( 5 - 1 ) = 10J$

In the given P-V graph, the process is clockwise. So, the work done will be positive which means that the system is doing the work.

questions.q:
For three low density gases $A, B, C$ pressure versus temperature graphs are plotted while keeping them at constant volume, as shown in the figure

The temperature corresponding to the point $' K '$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In case of& constant volume process, i.e., isochoric process,&

From ideal gas equation,

$\dfrac{P}{T} = n\dfrac{R}{V} =$constant

Or we have,~$P = \dfrac{nR}{V} \left(t + 273\right)$

If~$P = 0 ⇒ t = - 273 ° C$

Thus, when temperature goes to $- 273 ° C$, all constituent particles get freezed and pressure goes to zero irrespective of the density of gas.

Hence, the temperature corresponding to the point~$K = - 273 ° C.

$

questions.q: One mole of an ideal gas passes through a process where pressure and volume obey the relation $P = {P}_{o} \left[1 - \dfrac{1}{2}{ \left(\dfrac{{V}_{o}}{V}\right)}^{2}\right] .$Here ${P}_{o}$ and ${V}_{o}$ are constants. Calculate the change in the temperature of the gas if its volume changes from ${V}_{o}$ to $2{V}_{o}$ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For ideal gas, $PV = nRT$
Therefore, $\dfrac{nRT}{V} = {P}_{0} \left[$1 - \dfrac{1}{2}{ \left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{V}\right)}^{2}\right]$
$⇒ T = $\dfrac{{P}_{0}V}{R} \left[$1 - $\dfrac{1}{2}{ \left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{V}\right)}^{2}\right]
Therefore, the change in temperature is:
$\Delta T = {T}_{f} - {T}_{i}$
$= \dfrac{{P}_{0}\left({2V}_{0}\right)}{R}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{{2V}_{0}}\right)}^{2}\right) - \dfrac{{P}_{0}V}{R} \left(1 - $\dfrac{{V}_{0}^{2}}{2{V}_{0}^{2}}\right)
$= \dfrac{{5P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{4R}

questions.q:
A vertical closed cylinder is separated into two parts by a frictionless piston of mass $m$ and of negligible thickness. The piston is free to move along the length of the cylinder. The length of the cylinder above piston is ${l}_{1},$ and that below the piston is ${l}_{2},$ such that ${l}_{1} > {l}_{2} .$ Each part of the cylinder contains $n$ moles of an ideal gas at equal temperature $T .$ If the piston is stationary, its mass~$m$~will be given by:

($R$ is universal gas constant and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${P}_{1} + \dfrac{mg}{A} = {P}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{nRT}{{l}_{1}A} + \dfrac{mg}{A} = \dfrac{nRT}{{l}_{2}A}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{nRT}{g} \left(\dfrac{1}{{l}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{l}_{1}}\right)

$= $\dfrac{nRT}{g} \left(\dfrac{{l}_{1} - {l}_{2}}{{l}_{1}{l}_{2}}\right)

$

questions.q: Under an adiabatic process, the volume of an ideal gas gets doubled. Consequently, the mean collision time between the gas molecule changes from ${τ}_{1}$ to ${τ}_{2}$ . If $\dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{v}} = \gamma$ for this gas then a good estimate for $\dfrac{{τ}_{2}}{{τ}_{1}}$ is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relaxation time \left(τ\right) ∝ \dfrac{V}{T}$
And $T ∝ \dfrac{1}{V\gamma - 1}$
$τ ∝ V^{1 + \dfrac{\gamma - 1}{2}}$
$τ ∝ V\dfrac{1 + \gamma}{2}$
$\dfrac{{τ}_{f}}{{τ}_{i}} = {\left(\dfrac{2V}{V}\right)}^{\dfrac{\gamma + 1}{2}}$
$\dfrac{{τ}_{f}}{{τ}_{i}} = {\left(2\right)}^{\dfrac{\gamma + 1}{2}}

questions.q: The thermodynamic process, in which internal energy of the system remains constant is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
An isothermal process is& a thermodynamic process in which the temperature of a system remains constant. The transfer of heat into or out of the system happens so slowly that thermal equilibrium is maintained.

& $\Delta T = 0, \Delta U = n{C}_{V} ∆ T = 0$.

According to first law of thermodynamics,

$∆ Q = ∆ U + ∆ W ⇒ ∆ Q = ∆ W$

questions.q:
A sample of gas at temperature $T$ is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. Adiabatic constant for the gas is $\gamma=3 / 2$. The work done by the gas in the process is:
$(\mu=1 \mathrm{~mole})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}=\frac{\mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}}{1-\gamma} \\ & \mathrm{TV}^{\gamma-1}=\text { constan } \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}(2 \mathrm{~V})^{\gamma-1} \\ & \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{T}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 2}=\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \mathrm{~W}=\frac{\mathrm{R}\left(\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\sqrt{2}}-\mathrm{T}\right)}{1-\frac{3}{2}}=2 \mathrm{RT} \frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & =\mathrm{RT}(2-\sqrt{2})\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $One mole of an ideal gas is taken through an adiabatic process where the temperature rises from $27 ° C$ to $37 ° C$. If the ideal gas is composed of polyatomic molecule that has 4 vibrational modes, which of the following is true?  \left[R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}k^{- 1}\right]$
options: work done by the gas is close to $332J$
work done on the gas is close to $582J$
work done by the gas is close to $582J$
work done on the gas is close to $332J$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since, each vibrational mode, corresponds to two degrees of freedom, hence, $f =3 ( trans .) +3( rot . )+8( vib . )=14$

$ \text{ and } \gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f}$

$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{14} = \dfrac{8}{7}$

$W = \dfrac{nR\Delta T}{\gamma - 1} = - 582$

As $W < 0$. work is done on the gas.

questions.q: The total internal energy of two mole monoatomic ideal gas at temperature $T = 300K$ will be _____~$J$. (Given $R = 8 . 31J{mol}^{- 1} \cdot K$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The internal energy& of an ideal gas is a state function and is given by,& $U = n{C}_{v}T$.

For monatomic gas,~${C}_{v} = \dfrac{3}{2}R$.

Therefore,~$U = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times 8 . 31 \times 300 = 7479J$

questions.q: An ideal gas initially at $0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ temperature, is compressed suddenly to one fourth of its volume. If the ratio of specific heat at constant pressure to that at constant volume is $3 / 2$, the change in temperature due to the thermodynamic process is _____ K.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \gamma=\frac{3}{2} \\ & \mathrm{Tv}^{\gamma-1}=\mathrm{C} \\ & 273 \mathrm{~V}_0^{0.5}=\mathrm{T}\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{4}\right)^{0.5} \\ & \mathrm{~T}=273 \times 2=546 \\ & \Delta \mathrm{~T}=273\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a certain thermodynamical process, the pressure of a gas depends on its volume as $kV^{3}$. The work done when the temperature changes from $100 ° C$ to $300 ° C$ will be $xnR$~where $n$ denotes number of moles of a gas find~$x$& ;
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P = kV^{3}$

${T}_{i} = 100 ° C \text{ and } {T}_{f} = 300 ° C$

$\Delta T = 300 - 100$

$\Delta T = 200 ° C$

$P = kV^{3}$

now~$PV = nRT$

$∴ kV^{4} = nRT$

now~$4kV^{3}dV = nRdT$

$∴ PdV = nRdT / 4$

$∴$ Work $= ∫ PdV = ∫ \dfrac{nRdT}{4} = \dfrac{nR}{4}\Delta T$

$= \dfrac{200}{4} \times nR = 50nR$

questions.q: Starting at temperature $300K,$ one mole of an ideal diatomic gas  \left(\gamma = 1.4\right)$ is first compressed adiabatically from volume ${V}_{1}$ to ${V}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{16} .$ It is then allowed to expand isobarically to volume $2{V}_{2}$ . If all the processes are the quasi-static then the final temperature of the gas (in ${}^{o}K$ ) is (to the nearest integer) ___________.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$PV^{y} = constant$
$TV^{- 1} = constant$
$300{\left({V}_{1}\right)}^{1.4 - 1} = {T}_{B}{\left(\dfrac{{V}_{1}}{16}\right)}^{2 / 5}$
${T}_{B} = 300 \times {2}^{8 / 5}$
Now for BC process
$\dfrac{{V}_{B}}{{T}_{B}} = \dfrac{{V}_{c}}{{T}_{c}}$
${T}_{c} = \dfrac{{V}_{c}{T}_{B}}{{v}_{B}} = 2 \times 300 \times {2}^{8 / 5}$
${T}_{c} = 1818.859$
${T}_{c} = 1819K$

questions.q:
The volume& $V$ of a given mass of monoatomic gas changes with temperature~$T$ according to the relation $V = KT\dfrac{2}{3}$. The workdone when temperature changes by~$90K$~will be $xR$. The value of $x$~is
[$R$& universal gas constant ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$We know that work done is& $W = ∫ PdV . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ P = $\dfrac{nRT}{V} . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ W = ∫ $\dfrac{nRT}{V}$dv . . . \left(3\right)$

and~$V = KT^{2 / 3} . . . \left(4\right)$

$⇒ W = ∫ $\dfrac{nRT}{KT^{2 / 3}} \cdotdv . . . \left(5\right)$

$⇒$ from \left(4\right): dv = \dfrac{2}{3}KT^{- 1 / 3}dT$

$⇒ W = {∫}_{T1}^{T2}\dfrac{nRT}{KT^{2 / $3}}\d$dfrac{2}{3}K\dfrac{1}{T^{1 / 3}}$dT$

$⇒ W = $\dfrac{2}{3}$nR \times \left({T}_{2} - {T}_{1}\right) . . . \left($6\right)$

$⇒ {T}_{2} - {T}_{1} = 90K . . . \left($7\right)$

$⇒ W = \dfrac{2}{3}nR $\times$90$

$⇒ W = 60nR$

Assuming $1$~mole of gas

$n = 1$

So $W = 60R$

$
